A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLDM study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original navigation experiments, success rates, trajectory analyses, ablations, and timing measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original navigation experiments and reports revised baseline results, additional replanning evaluations, and adapted TD-MPC2 comparisons.

M1.justification: PLDM retains the same architectures, JEPA prediction objective, collapse-prevention losses, predictor ensembles, and MPPI planning procedure. The model details match across v2 Appendix C and v4 Appendix D; ensemble-index notation is clarified.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same 23-dataset navigation study, including Two-Rooms data variations, Diverse PointMaze layout generalization, Ant-U-Maze stitching, and chaser avoidance. The added comparisons remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Appendix G and Table 6 add reward-free adaptations of TD-MPC2 and TD-MPC2 with inverse dynamics modeling. The six main methods, adapted DreamerV3, reconstruction baseline, and chasing-task Random/Zero comparators remain.

E3.justification: Appendix J substantially revises reported GCIQL and HIQL settings across Two-Rooms and Diverse PointMaze. For example, GCIQL's BC coefficient changes from 0.3 to 0.003 for most Two-Rooms settings, and HIQL's learning rate changes from 3e-4 to 3e-5 for short sequences. Appendix F.1 also extends replanning-frequency controls across dataset sweeps.

E4.justification: v4 extends the existing planning-time analysis with Figures 10–11, testing performance when replanning every four steps across Two-Rooms and Diverse PointMaze conditions. It also tests whether inverse dynamics modeling mitigates adapted TD-MPC2 collapse. Existing loss-component, ensemble, and HILP representation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The maze-generalization plot changes its uncertainty bands from standard deviation in v2 Figure 1 to standard error in v4 Figure 2, retaining three seeds. v4 explicitly discloses one seed for TD-MPC2+IDM. The pooled Welch tests and selected ten-seed analyses already existed in v2.

E6.justification: With revised baseline settings, Table 2 replaces GCIQL's no-door-passing success rate of 22.0 ± 1.4 with 99.6 ± 0.4. Figures 4 and 6 substantially revise GCIQL and HIQL rankings, and Tables 7–8 no longer report significant PLDM superiority over GCIQL in the Two-Rooms comparisons. New results include replanning controls and adapted TD-MPC2 success rates of 0%, or 35% with IDM.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, training and planning objectives, collapse-prevention mathematics, and layout-distance definition remain substantively unchanged. Notational corrections do not introduce new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract retracts a central comparative advantage: v2 claims better trajectory stitching, whereas v4 describes stitching comparable to leading model-free methods. The conclusion also softens superior data efficiency to a high level of data efficiency, while retaining PLDM's layout-generalization advantage.

C2.justification: Sections 4.3–4.5 recognize GCIQL as competitive and revise explanations of GCRL failures, including a dynamic-programming hypothesis for short-trajectory stitching. Section 4.7 adds a hierarchical-control explanation for HIQL's Ant performance. v4 also explicitly qualifies task transfer by fixed dynamics and discusses the adapted Dreamer comparison's limitations and PLDM's inference cost.

D1.justification: Appendix J substantially expands baseline reproducibility information with grid-search procedures, dataset-specific goal-sampling and BC/AWR settings, and Ant-U-Maze baseline tables absent from v2. v4 also supplies a direct PLDM repository link and describes its environment, data-generation, training, and evaluation scripts; v2 already announced a code/data release through its project page.

R1.justification: v4 adds the TD-MPC2 citation and discusses its reward-dependent representation learning relative to PLDM's setting. It also qualifies its positioning against adapted DreamerV3. The broader related-work coverage remains essentially unchanged; numerical citation formatting is a presentation change.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain. v4 revises headings, explanatory paragraphs, and takeaways, uses more precise layout terminology, adds appendix navigation and acknowledgments, and relocates limitations and computational-cost discussions.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a different conference layout throughout, swaps the introductory figures, revises the overview graphic and plot markers, adds a main-text trajectory illustration and Figures 10–11, and restructures baseline hyperparameter tables. Existing appendix trajectory, ensemble, and HILP visualizations are retained and repositioned.

improvement.justification: The revised baseline settings and results materially strengthen this comparative study: v4 recognizes GCIQL's strong stitching and sample efficiency and HIQL's Ant performance, correcting important overgeneralizations in v2's argument. Narrower claims, expanded reproducibility information, and additional replanning controls improve the evidence's usefulness. The added TD-MPC2 comparison remains limited by its adaptation and single-seed IDM result, but the decisive improvement is the more balanced central comparison.
